label: prf:curvature-rank-gb-stratification
title: Proof of curvature rank gb stratification
html:
Proof.

Step 1: F generates the GB rewrite ideal. The two-sided ideal I \subset \mathbb{C}\langle \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}\rangle generated by \{R_H(i)\}_{i=1}^{n-1} \cup \{R_{YB}(i)\}_{i=1}^{n-2} is exactly the kernel of the surjection

  \mathbb{C}\langle \sigma_i\rangle \twoheadrightarrow H_n(R, q), \quad
  H_n(R, q) = \mathbb{C}\langle \sigma_i\rangle / I.

By construction F takes values in I: F(\sigma_i, \sigma_j) \in I for every generator pair, and the Leibniz extension preserves I as an ideal. Therefore F is the universal curvature 2-cocycle for the GB rewrite system.

Step 2: GB filtration is generated by powers of I. The Bergman GB normal-form theorem (Hecke normal form) gives an explicit basis of H_n(R, q) as ascending products \sigma_{i_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k} with i_1 < i_2 < \cdots and bounded multiplicities. Writing any T_w as a free-algebra word, the GB rewriting algorithm reduces T_w to normal form by applying R_H, R_{YB} repeatedly. The filtration J^\ell(q) collects elements requiring at least \ell applications of these relations to reach normal form.

Gap. The ideal-power reading of J^\bullet — "J^\ell is the image of I^\ell under the quotient map" — is false, and Step 1 above is what refutes it: Step 1 establishes I = \ker\pi for \pi : \mathbb{C}\langle\sigma_i\rangle \twoheadrightarrow H_n(R,q), so \pi(I) = 0 and therefore \pi(I^\ell) = 0 for every \ell \geq 1 — the ideal-power filtration is identically zero above degree 0, and cannot stratify anything. Proved sorry-free as QOU.BraidKnot.WordFiltration.map_pow_eq_bot.

Step 3 below reads J^\bullet this way, so Step 3 is incomplete as it stands. Two further readings of J^\bullet present elsewhere in the corpus also fail — see docs/audits/2026-08-16-three-gb-filtrations-one-name.md.

Step 3: F^{\,r} measures rewrite depth. By the Leibniz rule and Step 1, F^{\,r}(T_w) \in I^r but F^{\,r-1}(T_w) \not\in I^r when T_w requires exactly r GB reductions. Combined with Step 2, F^{\,r}(T_w) \in J^r, F^{\,r-1}(T_w) \not\in J^r, so the curvature-rank r(T_w) as defined matches the GB filtration depth.

Step 4: Spectral sequence pages stratify by curvature-rank. The GB spectral sequence (GB spectral sequence) has E_0^{\ell, *} = J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} as the associated graded. By Step 3, this is exactly the curvature-rank-\ell stratum. The differentials d_r propagate elements between adjacent strata, and E_\infty^{\ell, *} is the stable cohomology at depth \ell, depending only on the curvature-rank-\ell residues. \square

Corollary (six-term mass formula = curvature-rank decomposition). By unified knot mass the six-term mass decomposes over E_\infty^{\ell, *}, and by the proposition each page corresponds to a curvature-rank stratum:

See Table.

Each term is the non-abelian Stokes residue at the corresponding curvature-rank stratum of the GB filtration spectral sequence, paired with the Markov-trace functional.

Witness. the formal derivation and the formal derivation identify hyperbolic-knot ideals at specific GB positions for the proton and neutron braids. The neutron's extra ideal at (GB depth 3, jet 1, std channel) — the 6_1 knot — is the curvature-rank-3 std-stratum residue that is structurally absent from the proton. This residue is the algebraic origin of the proton-neutron mass splitting at the Hochschild-cohomology level.
